title.narrative: UNICEF WASH Strengthening Community Resilience to COVID-19 and Climate Shocks
UNICEF WASH Stärkt motståndskraft mot Covid-19 och klimatchocker

description.narrative:
The overall goal of phase I was to reduce the risk of COVID-19 infection in the informal settlements of Nairobi and Nakuru though improved access to sustainable WASH services and hygiene practices.
Outcome 1. Provide access to safe drinking water in target communities and in health care facilities
Outcome 2. Provide access to sanitation and hygiene services in target informal settlements
Outcome 3. Community sensitization on appropriate hygiene practices (including COVID-19 prevention and Menstrual Hygiene Management )
Outcome 4. Enhanced coordination and monitoring of WASH COVID-19 response
The overall goal of phase II was to strengthen community resilience to COVID-19 in informal settlements of Nairobi County and climate shocks in drought-prone Samburu County through improved access to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services.
Outcome 1. 170,000 people gain access to WASH services in informal settlements of Nairobi County
Outcome 2. 45,000 people have access to climate resilient and sustained WASH services and community climate resilience is strengthened in Samburu County

Bidrag till UNICEFs intervention, via Vatten, Sanitet och Hygien-sektorn, till åtgärder mot COVID-19 i Kenya 2019/2020, i gränssnittet mellan humanitärt och och långsiktigt utvecklingsarbete; Vattenförsörjning för att förebygga och kontrollera smitta, sanitet och hygien, informationsarbete för nya hygien-normer, samt förbättrad samordning av externt stöd till Kenya inom vatten, sanitet och hygien under COVID-19-krisen. En del av insatsen kommer att genomföras av UNICEF själva, andra genomföras av tredje part, dels genom upphandling, dels genom vidareförmedling. Insatsen är en påbyggnad på redan pågående UNICEF-program, med inarbetade rutiner, och risken i genomförandet anses genomgående låg. För sanitets- och hygien komponenten har den lokala organisationen Sanergy redan identifierats genom ansökningsförfarande.

UNICEF component on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene sector response to COVID-19 in Kenya 2019/2020, in the HUM/ development nexus; Water supply to prevent and control infection, Sanitation & Hygiene, community sensitation for new social norms for hygiene behaviour, and support to improved coordination of external support to Kenya in WASH during the COVID-19 crisis.
Part of the programme will be implemented by UNICEF themselves, others will be implemented by third parties. either through procurement, or through forwarding of funds. The programme is an add-on to already existing UNICEF initiatives in the sector, with existing routines, and the implementation risk is generally seen as low. For the Sanitation & Hygiene Component, the local organisation Sanergy has already been identified through application procedure.

sector.narrative: Basic drinking water supply and basic sanitation

description.narrative:
Phase 1 results examples
128,000 people at community level gained access to safe drinking water through the completion of 29 out of 27 water kiosks and 25 out of 25 yard-taps in the communities, representing 324% of the target population of 39,500 people. In health care facilities, the installation of elevated water storage tanks, drinking water points, and hand washing station were completed in 33 out of 30 facilities (110%), benefiting 129,717 people.
3,432 container-based toilets were fully operationalized reaching at total of 113,088 people, with 100% of the pit waste being collected, treated, and converted into end-products. A newly constructed discharge centre is in place and finishing works have been completed and launched. A total of 134,314 people benefited from the distribution of essential WASH supplies, including soap, hand sanitizer, hand washing stations, surface disinfectants, and personal protection equipment (PPE). 116% of the target was achieved. A total of 510 hand washing stations were installed in public spaces and in use.
In total, 712,078 people (385,823 in Nairobi and 326,255 in Nakuru) were reached through the in-person community sensitization activities against the against the target of 225,000 people (316% of the target achieved). The project also provided MHM kits to 5,435 adolescent girls and women from the most vulnerable households along with training sessions on menstrual hygiene education. Furthermore, a total of 832,367 people (696,177 in Nairobi and 136,190 in Nakuru) were reached through a social media advocacy on COVID-19 prevention and MHM.
Phase II results examples
The rehabilitation of five water kiosks provided access to daily safe drinking water services to 12,500 people in communities of Mathare and Mukuru informal settlements, while the connection and storage improvement works for 15 health facilities reached 42,000 people that fall in the catchments areas of those health care facilities in the same informal settlements of Nairobi, resulting in a total of 54,500 people gaining improved access to safe drinking water, against a target of 20,000 people. The Water Kiosks have storage facilities and are equipped with ATM system that provides 24hour access to water at affordable rates of Kes 0.5 cents per 20lt.
Furthermore, UNICEF has provided daily access to safely managed sanitation to 196,898 people (against a target of 170,000 people) in the two Nairobi informal settlements (Mukuru and Mathare) through a network of 5,958 active container based toilets in partnership with Sanergy (Freshlife). The network of these low cost toilets has contributed to improving human health and well being and the surrounding natural environment. The full sanitation value chain is being addressed. The waste collection service safely removes 2,631 metric tons of waste monthly from these toilets which is converted to energy, fertilizer, and insect protein for animal feed. Due to high demand of the full sanitation service chain in the crowded informal settlements, the target was exceeded.
The floods in May 2024 had a significant impact on sanitation services, critical in preventing environmental contamination and maintaining public health, especially in densely populated Nairobi informal settlements. The network of 5,958 container-based toilets is less susceptible to floods and therefore this project contributed to mitigating flood impacts by preventing environmental contamination otherwise caused by overflowed pit waste and open defecation, through ensuring safe waste collection services in Mukuru and Mathare informal settlements.
Building on the successful collaboration with Huru International Kenya in phase I which was continued in phase II, 10,000 girls (100% of the target) received reusable Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) kits and education. As a result, girls dignity and self esteem has been upheld and they are able to attend school contributing to improvement of their academic performance. Huru International model integrates the skill building of girls and women in informal settlements on tailoring, including making hygienic reusable sanitary pads, to respond to the market needs in their neighbourhoods. The partner further implemented community sensitization activities on COVID-19 prevention and MHM in informal settlements of Nairobi and 131,246 people (against a target of 120,000 people) (75,169 women and 56,077 men) have been reached and sensitized on this important topic. As a result, the community members have increased awareness on COVID-19 prevention practices especially hand washing with water and soap. This has also contributed to reduction of water related diseases due to improved hygiene practices at the community and household level, especially during the recent floods that impacted the informal settlements heavily.
Access to climate resilient and sustained WASH services in Samburu County
At the end of the project 28,900 people (6092 men, 6220 women, 8116 boys and 8472 girls), were reached with access to climate resilient water supply services. This is a result of the construction of three sand dams and installation of water abstraction hand pumps, as well as the rehabilitation and upgrading of nine boreholes to solar pumping systems. To ensure sustainability, capacity building of several government entities (Water User Associations (WUAs), Water Resources Associations (WRUAs) and officials) on proper management of water services, best hygiene practices, integrated water management and climate resilience planning, was also executed.
For the WASH in school component, UNICEF met the target to provide 15 schools with gender and disability sensitive sanitation facilities, hygiene promotion (including Menstrual Hygiene Management) and capacity building of Boards of Management (BOM) on sustainable operation and maintenance of the WASH facilities. The construction works are complete in all 15 schools benefiting a total of 8,840 (4547 boys and 4293 girls) school going children. On capacity building, 45 teachers were trained and 44 BoMs members were trained on hygiene promotion (including MHM) as well as Operation and Maintenance of the WASH facilities in schools.
The water audit and development of cloud based database for the three sub counties in Samburu County was completed. Rural Focus Limited was contracted to carry out full assessment of the water sources including equipped and nonequipped sources and develop the database in Samburu County. This detailed audit report has provided critical information for planning, investment and service delivery including management models for water supply systems. Notably, according to the audit, over one third of Samburus water points are still non functional.
To increase access to sanitation, UNICEF conducted a series of consultative meetings with the National and County MoH to set a target and identify geographical locations to deliver 150 villages to Open Defecation Free (ODF) certified status, targeting 45,000 people living in safe and clean environment in Samburu. At project end, all the 150 targeted villages have been triggered, claimed, verified, and certified as ODF, enabling 45,000 people to gain access to sanitation and have improved hygiene practices including hand washing with soap.
Through the Zuhura Impact partnership, a Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship Curriculum for young social innovators, aged between 18 and 24 years, with a particular focus on young women and youth from Samburu County was designed. Through the project, 75 young people have been trained and started green businesses. The winning 5 teams have been supported with a longer trajectory, and got mentorship, seed funding and incubation. All 5 teams have established green (agricultural) businesses and have done their first harvests. This has contributed to improved livelihoods and food security for communities in drought prone Samburu.
Additionally, the Samburu County Disaster Risk Reduction Bill and Policy was finalized to enhance climate resilience and disaster management. It improves emergency preparedness, enables rapid response, secures funding through a dedicated disaster management fund, promotes stakeholder coordination, and aligns with global standards protecting lives and livelihoods while fostering sustainable development and resilience.
